text:
Maya (CSM): Heads up — MapleTech (Eli) raised an ask: they plan to onboard three teams (Realtime Search, Customer Insights, Documentation QA) over the next 8 weeks and want to stream webhook events into embeddings. They also expect heavy month-end summarization jobs.
Eli (MapleTech): Hi all, we're ramping fast. Expect ~30-50k embeddings/day and spikes up to ~600 qps during reporting windows. Realtime Search needs low-latency streaming responses for live operator UI. What's feasible in hosted vs dedicated?
Luca (AM): Renewal window in 4 months. This looks like an expansion opportunity. Eli, would you consider committing to reserved capacity if we can guarantee latency for Realtime Search?
Eli (MapleTech): Potentially yes. We'd like a pricing estimate for a small dedicated pool for Search + hosted embeddings for other teams. Also need recommendations for batching webhook ingestion.
Rina (Solutions): @Maya can you share expected payload sizes? For streaming, what is the avg token length and whether generated completions are short or multi-turn?
Maya (CSM): Eli sent sample metrics: embeddings payloads 200-800 tokens, avg 450; search generation avg 150 tokens, interactive. They prefer p50 <250ms for UI.
Sam (Infra): 250ms p50 on hosted for interactive gen at that token length is tight. Recommend: option A) Dedicated small pool (1 GPU card equivalent) with autoscale to 3 for bursts; option B) Hosted with traffic shaping + fallback. For embeddings, enable batching and async ingest workers.
Jordan (Support): We'll need to prepare a webhook failure runbook and a template for replaying dropped events. Also schedule two 45-min onboarding sessions per team (integration + ops).
Rina (Solutions): Drafting tech plan: - Dedicated for Realtime Search (SSE or websocket streaming support) - Hosted embeddings with prefix caching and compact quantized model for Docs QA - A short migration guide for webhook backpressure handling.
Sam (Infra): Quick config snippet for autoscale and batching (pseudo):
```yaml
service: realtime-search
autoscale:
  min: 1
  max: 3
  target_qps: 200
batching:
  enabled: true
  max_tokens: 4096
cache:
  kv_prefix: true
  ttl: 1800
```
Luca (AM): I'll prepare a commercial ballpark: dedicated pool + burst = estimated +30% ARR uplift during contract. Need finance to confirm. Eli, would that be in your budget range?
Eli (MapleTech): Sounds reasonable, need the exact numbers. Also ask: can we have per-route dashboards and token-level cost breakdown for their internal billing?
Maya (CSM): Yes, per-route metrics and cost attribution available in Console. I'll include that in the enablement.
Jordan (Support): I'll create the onboarding calendar and invite MapleTech engineers.
billing-bot: Note: create provisional quote ID QT-2048 for MapleTech expansion request.
Maya (CSM): Action items: 1) Sam to run capacity calc and provide latency feasibility by tomorrow EOD (Sam) 2) Rina to produce tech recommendation doc (Rina) 3) Luca to draft preliminary pricing and contract options (Luca) 4) Jordan to schedule workshops (Jordan).
Sam (Infra): Running calc now — initial estimate: dedicated 1-card pool with autoscale + hosted embeddings with batching should meet p50 target for most interactive queries; will post numbers.
Eli (MapleTech): Appreciate the quick response. We'll prioritize Search first and then bring Analytics and Docs online. Looking forward to the workshops.
Maya (CSM): Thanks team — I'll update the renewal forecast and mark this as a high expansion opportunity. Will post a follow-up thread with the calculation results. :rocket:
